subject: Re: Freedom of Information / Historical Records Request - Mr. Williams, Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department, 1897 Marconi Lavernock Experiments
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Information Governance Team,

Thank you for your response. To whom am I speaking?

I note your advice that Glamorgan Archives may be the appropriate
repository for historic material. I will contact Glamorgan Archives
separately.

However, I would like to clarify that my request was not limited to
deposited historical archive material.

My request concerns any recorded information held by Cardiff Council and
its predecessor authorities relating to Great House Farm, Llandough (Ty
Mawr), including operational records created or retained by the Council.

Please confirm:

Which Cardiff Council departments were consulted before reaching the
conclusion that Glamorgan Archives was the appropriate route;

Whether searches were carried out within:
- Planning records;
- Building Control records;
- Legal Services records;
- Estates/property records;
- Highways records;
- Environmental/archaeology records;
- Records inherited from former Glamorgan County Council or South Glamorgan
County Council;
- Whether the following search terms were used:

"Great House Farm"
"Ty Mawr"
"Llandough"
"Buckler"
"Williams"
"BP Properties"
"BP Pension Trust"
"Western Ground Rents"

Whether Cardiff Council holds any records relating to:
- the demolition of Great House Farm around 1988;
- planning and development of the replacement housing;
- any inspections, surveys, photographs or reports concerning the site;
- correspondence with BP, their representatives, the Buckler/Williams
family, Cadw, archaeological bodies or other public authorities.

I appreciate Glamorgan Archives may hold historic deposited collections.
However, an archive referral does not confirm whether Cardiff Council
itself holds related administrative records, and I would therefore be
grateful for confirmation of the searches undertaken before this request is
redirected.

Given the age and significance of the records concerned, I would appreciate
this clarification at your earliest convenience.

Kind regards,

Requester (Ret'd Sgt)
 & Life Member

> Dear Information Rights / Archives Team,
>
> I am writing to request information under the Freedom of Information Act
> 2000 (or equivalent records access) regarding my grandfather, Mr. Williams,
> who worked in the engineering department of the Cardiff Post Office /
> General Post Office around 1897.
>
> Specifically, I seek any records, personnel files, correspondence,
> reports, or mentions confirming his involvement in Guglielmo Marconi’s
> wireless telegraphy experiments at Lavernock Point (including erecting the
> 120-foot pole and related tests to Flat Holm). This relates to contemporary
> newspaper reports from May 1897.
>
> Please provide:
>
>    - Any personnel or service records for Mr. Williams in the Cardiff
>    engineering department circa 1897.
>    - Documents referencing "Mr. Williams" in connection with Marconi’s
>    demonstrations.
>    - Any other relevant historical files from the GPO
>    telegraph/engineering teams.
>
> My full name: Requester Address: [address redacted], Vale of
> Glamorgan, [postcode redacted]
> [map link redacted]
> Contact: [email redacted] Relationship: Great Grandson
>
> I am ultimately seeking any record about my great grandfather Mr Williams
> of Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff (formerly Vale of Glamorgan). Not
> to be confused with Great House Farm, Llandough, Cowbridge, Vale of
> Glamorgan. And his role in the Marconi experiment. And before and after
> Marconis stay with our family in our home in 1897.
>
> I am happy to provide further identification if required. Thank you for
> your assistance.
>
> Best regards,
>
> Requester
